transcript.text: Hi everyone, thanks for being here. Before I can approve the delivery package for our Harbor Film Festival premiere, I need to run the routine rights and technical signoff round. I'd like to hear from our clearance counsel and post-production supervisor on any constraints or required delivery changes related to the current draft — that includes the in-person screening, the possible festival livestream, the standard music credit, and the stereo audio master. Who'd like to go first?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I have some important constraints to report from the rights side. I confirmed with the publisher this morning that the signed license for 'Blue Hour' permits only the in-person festival screening — it prohibits a livestream. Additionally, the license requires the exact credit line: "Song 'Blue Hour' written by Nia Cole, published by Northstar Music" — so the standard music credit currently in the draft won't suffice. I haven't entered this confirmation in the delivery tracker yet because the publisher's email is still being attached to the clearance file, but I wanted to flag these issues now during the signoff round.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to report a critical technical constraint. My venue ingest test confirmed yesterday that the Harbor Film Festival accepts this title only as a 5.1 discrete DCP mastered at 24 fps. The current stereo audio master in our delivery draft is rejected. I haven't sent the test report to Mara yet because it's still in the post-production technical folder awaiting the final export log, but this means we need to replace the stereo master with a 5.1 DCP at 24 fps before approval.
transcript.speaker: A3
